~~~python~~~
import pandas as pd

# Create the dataframe from the provided table
data = {
    'home team': ['footscray', 'fitzroy', 'essendon', 'carlton', 'hawthorn', 'collingwood'],
    'home team score': ['14.7 (91)', '16.14 (110)', '13.12 (90)', '20.8 (128)', '19.14 (128)', '10.13 (73)'],
    'away team': ['st kilda', 'north melbourne', 'richmond', 'south melbourne', 'geelong', 'melbourne'],
    'away team score': ['9.11 (65)', '9.12 (66)', '17.9 (111)', '8.15 (63)', '15.8 (98)', '8.10 (58)'],
    'venue': ['western oval', 'junction oval', 'windy hill', 'princes park', 'glenferrie oval', 'vfl park'],
    'crowd': [18655, 7007, 22251, 14465, 12425, 30883],
    'date': ['15 july 1972', '15 july 1972', '15 july 1972', '15 july 1972', '15 july 1972', '15 july 1972']
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Extract the numeric score from the 'away team score' column
# The numeric part is inside parentheses, e.g., "9.11 (65)" -> 65
df['away_score_numeric'] = df['away team score'].str.extract(r'\((\d+)\)').astype(int)

# Count total number of away teams
total_away_teams = len(df)

# Count away teams with score > 10
away_teams_gt_10 = (df['away_score_numeric'] > 10).sum()

# Check if 1/3 of away teams have score > 10
# Use exact fraction: 1/3 * total_away_teams
required_count = (1/3) * total_away_teams
answer = away_teams_gt_10 >= required_count
